rejected_items.name: Legacy QueueService and StateService proto contracts

features.name: Passive pane observation and delta capture
features.notes: Use FrankenTerm's passive-first and gap-aware capture model to harden Lev's current capture/delta semantics.

features.name: Robot Mode JSON/TOON control envelope
features.lev_equivalent: No typed ft-compatible robot backend; AgentSession exposes TS methods only.
features.notes: Map state/get-text/send/wait-for/search/events envelopes to AgentSessionObservation and AgentSessionReceipt in a fake backend first.

features.name: Policy-gated reads, writes, approvals, and redaction
features.lev_equivalent: AgentSession guard receipts and Lev policy plane; no equivalent per-pane redaction/read policy envelope.
features.notes: Preserve Lev's policy ownership, but copy the envelope shape: read and write surfaces should both be policy-evaluated and receipt-bearing.

features.name: Search over captured terminal output
features.lev_equivalent: cass/qmd/index search exist, but no dedicated searchable terminal scrollback backend for AgentSession.
features.notes: Treat searchable scrollback as evidence storage/projection, not as FlowMind state.

features.name: Wait-for pattern semantics without sleep loops
features.lev_equivalent: AgentSession.wait currently polls capture with bounded attempts; managed-tmux has typed WAIT_PATTERN_TIMEOUT.
features.notes: Upgrade wait-for into event/pattern-driven semantics while retaining Lev's existing typed failure envelope.

features.name: Terminal platform as FlowMind spine
features.lev_equivalent: FlowMind control/policy plane plus Orchestration/Harness/Event Bus plane split.
features.notes: Rejected as a spine replacement because it would collapse policy, execution, eventing, and terminal substrate boundaries.

features.name: Robot family contracts with schema, side effects, and idempotency
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has contracts and flow specs, but no standard per-action-family contract pack for machine APIs.
features.notes: Apply the contract shape to AgentSession and FlowMind actions: schema, side effects, failure envelope, idempotency, conformance tests, and state-space proof.

features.name: Machine API parity across CLI, Robot Mode, and MCP
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has CLI and TypeScript APIs, but no single generated envelope shared across CLI JSON, robot calls, and MCP tools.
features.notes: Make ExecutionBinding/AgentSession receipts the canonical machine envelope before exposing any MCP bridge.

features.name: Stable error-code taxonomy for robot and MCP surfaces
features.lev_equivalent: Managed tmux has typed errors, but Lev lacks a cross-surface error-code matrix that maps CLI, graph, and MCP failures.
features.notes: Keep Lev's typed errors, but add a stable public code map for automation and dashboard consumers.

features.name: Read-path policy and redaction gates
features.lev_equivalent: Lev policies guard execution intent, but terminal reads and search projections do not yet have an explicit read-policy/redaction matrix.
features.notes: Apply to AgentSession.capture, search, event streams, diagnostics, and Graph projections so reads are policy-bearing too.

features.name: Approval impact simulation before side effects
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has approval and guard concepts, but no standard pre-effect impact simulator for terminal/session actions.
features.notes: Use this as the shape for AgentPing approvals: preview action, affected panes/files/work, policy reason, and rollback expectation before execution.

features.name: Policy audit chain, compliance, metrics, and quarantine
features.lev_equivalent: Lev records events and receipts, but policy outcomes are not yet promoted into an auditable compliance/quarantine chain.
features.notes: Apply by emitting durable policy-decision events with chain IDs, compliance dimensions, and quarantine state.

features.name: Event annotation, triage, label, mute, and dedupe
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has Event Bus and workstream state, but event lifecycle operations are spread across tools and not normalized.
features.notes: Promote event lifecycle mutations as graph operations: annotate, triage, label, mute, dedupe, and explain.

features.name: SSE event and delta streams with backpressure controls
features.lev_equivalent: AgentSession.observe exists, but no stable event/delta stream contract with max_hz, keepalive, and backpressure semantics.
features.notes: Use this for browser/dashboard and agent consumers so streaming terminal data cannot overwhelm the control plane.

features.name: Search explainability, index stats, and reindex controls
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has search tools and generated reports, but no terminal-capture search explain or index health contract.
features.notes: Apply to captured terminal/output evidence: every search result should be explainable and every index should report freshness.

features.name: Hybrid lexical, semantic, and reranked scrollback search
features.lev_equivalent: cass/qmd cover transcript/session search, but AgentSession scrollback is not yet a first-class hybrid-search corpus.
features.notes: Do not import the implementation; reuse the domain split for lexical exactness, semantic recall, rerank, and redacted snippets.

features.name: Pattern trigger engine over terminal output
features.lev_equivalent: AgentSession.wait polls for patterns, but pattern triggers are not durable event producers.
features.notes: Turn wait conditions into durable pattern-trigger events with IDs, evidence spans, and timeout reasons.

features.name: Reservations and leases for shared resources
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has workstreams and some lock/claim flows, but no unified reservation ledger for panes, files, work items, and agents.
features.notes: Apply to multi-agent Lev execution as a graph-backed lease system with expiry, owner, conflict reason, and release receipt.

features.name: Work claim/release/complete state machine
features.lev_equivalent: .lev workstreams encode lifecycle state, but execution-time work claims are not backed by a formal work state machine.
features.notes: Use this to harden Lev work assignment: ready, claim, heartbeat, release, complete, and stale-owner recovery.

features.name: Checkpoint state machine and durable session reentry
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has handoffs and transcript search, but AgentSession reentry is not yet a tested checkpoint family.
features.notes: Apply to resume chains: capture pane, context capsule, active work entity, last receipt, and replayable recovery action.

features.name: Context horizon and context budget contracts
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has context and token-budget concepts, but no shared context-horizon schema tied to runtime output capture.
features.notes: Apply to FlowMind ticks so context windows are explicit inputs with budget, freshness, omission, and rehydration semantics.

features.name: Encrypted and inspectable handoff capsules
features.lev_equivalent: Lev handoffs are durable markdown/YAML artifacts, but not a typed encrypted/inspectable capsule object.
features.notes: Keep Lev's readable workstream files, but add an optional capsule schema for portable resume bundles and sensitive session transfer.

features.name: Profile apply contracts for agent/runtime bootstrap
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has session profiles and substrate policy, but profile apply is not a robot-family operation with rollback/idempotency.
features.notes: Apply to tmux/headless session-profile activation: dry-run, validate, apply, rollback, and duplicate-request idempotency.

features.name: Agent detection, configure, list, and running surfaces
features.lev_equivalent: Lev can spawn and list sessions, but agent runtime discovery/configuration is not exposed as a normalized robot surface.
features.notes: Expose current sessions, supported agent types, runtime config, and detection evidence through one typed surface.

features.name: Fleet status, scale, rebalance, and health
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has native subagents and OMX teams, but no shared fleet health contract across local sessions and orchestration lanes.
features.notes: Adopt the health/scale/rebalance vocabulary for dashboards and future multi-lane Lev execution, without importing FrankenTerm fleet runtime.

features.name: Distributed agent mode with explicit stale/live-output boundary
features.lev_equivalent: Lev does not have a first-class remote-pane persistence model with live-output limitations spelled out.
features.notes: If Lev adds remote execution, copy the honesty: persisted state may be available when live pane capture is not.

features.name: Resource pressure and fleet memory controls
features.lev_equivalent: Lev budget controls are mostly task/token oriented; runtime memory, fd, and scrollback pressure are not first-class scheduling inputs.
features.notes: Feed resource pressure into admission, nudge, capture frequency, and shutdown policies for large agent runs.

features.name: Mission plan/run/status/explain/pause/resume/abort
features.lev_equivalent: FlowMind and workstreams can express plans, but mission runtime control is not exposed as one stateful operation family.
features.notes: Apply as FlowMind execution API shape: plan, run, status, explain, pause, resume, abort, and event stream.

features.name: Transactional execution with plan, run, rollback, and killswitch
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has receipts and gates, but cross-step rollback/compensation is not a standard execution primitive.
features.notes: Use for high-risk lanes: compile a transaction plan, declare compensations, run with receipts, and support operator killswitch.

features.name: Workflow descriptors and built-in wait/action handlers
features.lev_equivalent: FlowMind graphs and Lev workflows exist, but runtime workflow descriptors are not yet unified with AgentSession wait/action handlers.
features.notes: Apply by compiling FlowMind workflow steps into typed AgentSession operations with consistent wait, timeout, and event receipts.

features.name: Diagnostics bundle and reproduce export/replay
features.lev_equivalent: Lev verification outputs exist, but there is no one-command incident/reproduce bundle for session runtime failures.
features.notes: Add a bundle shape for AgentSession failures: config, events, redacted capture, receipts, policy decisions, and replay command.

features.name: Replay, forensics, and equivalence contracts
features.lev_equivalent: Lev can inspect transcripts, but runtime replay equivalence is not a tested contract.
features.notes: Define replayable evidence for terminal/session incidents and use it as a Pentagon verification corpus.

features.name: Incident autopsy and flight-recorder event schema
features.lev_equivalent: Lev event logs are not yet packaged as a flight-recorder stream with autopsy-ready schema.
features.notes: Use this as the durable event schema target for debugging FlowMind/orchestration/tmux failures.

features.name: Attestation manifests and release proof bundles
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has parity reports and validation gates, but release claims are not packaged as signed/structured attestation manifests.
features.notes: Apply to promotion gates: every runtime claim should have evidence path, verifier, scope, and retraction path.

features.name: Reality-check discipline for claim hygiene
features.lev_equivalent: Lev emphasizes evidence, but no standard claim-audit artifact is attached to parity/runtime promotions.
features.notes: Add claim hygiene to FlowMind/tmux promotions: verified, stale, assumed, blocked, or retracted.

features.name: Browser auth bootstrap flows for agent providers
features.lev_equivalent: Lev should not absorb provider auth mechanics into FlowMind; auth bootstrap belongs in environment/tooling boundaries.
features.notes: Reference for setup UX only; do not wire provider-specific browser auth into core FlowMind execution.

features.name: Account usage, cost tracking, and refresh contracts
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has token usage receipts in AgentSession, but no account-refresh/cost surface shared across providers.
features.notes: Apply by separating provider account state from execution receipts while linking usage to session/work IDs.

features.name: Config profiles and ruleset profiles
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has config files and substrate policies, but profile/ruleset evaluation is not exposed as list/show/test/lint robot calls.
features.notes: Apply to FlowMind/AgentSession policies with list, show, test, lint, and explain operations.

features.name: Saved searches and bookmarks over runtime evidence
features.lev_equivalent: Lev can search sessions, but saved search/bookmark state is not part of the runtime evidence model.
features.notes: Apply to dashboards and workstreams: save useful runtime queries and link them to decisions or incidents.

features.name: CASS and CAUT style session search and usage integration
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has cass as a local tool, but capture/search/usage are not wired into AgentSession as one evidence graph.
features.notes: Use Lev's existing cass strength, but make session runtime receipts discoverable from the same evidence graph.

features.name: Command guard and destructive-action policy
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has dcg and guardrails, but terminal send/prepare/commit are not all one guarded command lifecycle.
features.notes: Apply by routing send/prepare/commit through a single guard receipt with command class, risk, approval, and audit outcome.

features.name: Noise control, event mutes, and dedupe policy
features.lev_equivalent: Lev event reporting can become noisy during long runs; no reusable noise-control policy exists for runtime streams.
features.notes: Apply to rolling statuses and dashboards so repeated terminal patterns collapse without hiding new failures.

features.name: Capture overflow and backpressure policy
features.lev_equivalent: AgentSession capture currently lacks a documented overflow/backpressure behavior under high-output panes.
features.notes: Define drop/truncate/spill behavior explicitly and emit an evidence event whenever capture fidelity changes.

features.name: JSON schema corpus as generated conformance surface
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has TypeScript types and YAML specs, but no generated JSON schema corpus for robot/API consumers.
features.notes: Generate schemas from Lev contract types so CLI, Graph, dashboard, and MCP consumers verify the same envelopes.

features.name: Formal specs for risky robot families
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has validation gates, but few stateful execution families have TLA/StateRight-style transition proofs.
features.notes: Apply only to high-blast-radius Lev families: work claims, checkpoint/reentry, transactions, fleet admission, and policy quarantine.

features.name: Swarm capacity admission and herd-wave scheduling
features.lev_equivalent: Lev can spawn native subagents, but admission control is not resource-model-backed across large concurrent runs.
features.notes: Use for future team/autodev scaling: admit work in waves based on capacity, pressure, and expected output volume.

features.name: Latency budget algebra and verification catalog
features.lev_equivalent: Lev tracks budgets loosely, but no stage-level runtime latency budget algebra exists for terminal/session operations.
features.notes: Apply to capture, wait-for, search, event streaming, and dashboard projections with per-stage timing receipts.

features.name: Framework-neutral MCP DTOs and proxy controls
features.lev_equivalent: Lev connector work exists, but MCP DTOs/proxy mutability policy are not a shared core contract.
features.notes: If Lev exposes MCP, separate DTOs from runtime code and make mutating-tool allowance explicit.

features.name: Mux boundary truth and backend identity discipline
features.lev_equivalent: Lev already has ExecutionBinding, but custom tmux discussions can still blur backend contract vs implementation.
features.notes: Keep the lesson: call the backend what it is, hide it behind a real contract, and do not fake a generic abstraction before a second backend exists.

features.name: NTM capability census and cutover playbook discipline
features.lev_equivalent: Lev has parity registry and specs, but migration/cutover work does not always start from a capability census.
features.notes: Apply this exact pattern to any tmux-control replacement: census, preserve/upgrade/drop matrix, corpus, cutover gate, and rollback.

features.name: Town (workspace root ~/gt/)
features.notes: Lev XDG split is more compliant; gastown's flat ~/gt/ is intentional but breaks XDG.

features.name: Rig (per-project container around git repo)
features.notes: Same idea, lev names it differently.

features.name: Bead (atomic git-backed work unit, stored in Dolt)
features.notes: Lev has bd, but does not lean on it as universal substrate; gastown makes beads load-bearing.

features.name: Hook (pinned bead = agent's primary work queue)
features.lev_equivalent: no clean primitive — closest is herenow but herenow is context not work-pointer
features.notes:
Cleanest abstraction in gastown. Worth lifting verbatim. Lev should consider
a "hook" or "pinned task" primitive in dna/ — single per-agent work pointer.

features.name: Convoy (work-order grouping related beads)
features.notes: Lev workstream is heavier; convoy is lighter shovel-ready bundle.

features.name: GUPP (Gas Town Universal Propulsion Principle)
features.lev_equivalent: FlowMind autonomous-on-context model + dna/ constraint manifold
features.notes: Lev has the substance but lacks the named, agent-facing formulation.

features.name: MEOW (Molecular Expression of Work)
features.lev_equivalent: C1 Finitude + C2 Non-Commutation + entity granularity
features.notes: Decompose goals into atomic, trackable beads.

features.name: NDI (Nondeterministic Idempotence)
features.lev_equivalent: C4 ratchet (deferred), receipts — but no named NDI principle
features.notes: Worth a dna/ principle entry. C4 covers it conceptually but isn't kernel-enforced.

features.name: Role taxonomy (Mayor/Deacon/Witness/Refinery/Polecat/Crew/Dog)
features.lev_equivalent: no first-class role taxonomy — harness/team is partial
features.notes:
Lev has plugins/slate (swarm topology) and OMC teams skill but no DNA-rooted
role primitive. Consider dna/roles.yaml or borrow as-is.

features.name: Polecat (ephemeral worker with persistent CV)
features.lev_equivalent: tmux-harness session model is closest but lacks identity persistence
features.notes: Identity-vs-session split is sharper than lev's current model.

features.name: Crew (long-lived human/agent worker with own clone)
features.notes: Persistent worker with dedicated git clone, human-supervised.

features.name: Refinery (Bors-style bisecting merge queue)
features.notes:
Critical for multi-agent parallelism. Lev currently relies on humans
to merge; refinery is a real gap when scaling >2 concurrent workers.

features.name: Wasteland (federated multi-town network via DoltHub)
features.notes: Marked Planned in why-these-features.md:80,156 — gastown is also still building.

features.name: Seance (read-only fork into past session)
features.lev_equivalent: no clean primitive; partial via /handoff + workstream history
features.notes: Useful primitive for "what did past-me decide" without resuming.

features.name: Watchdog chain (Daemon→Boot→Deacon→Witness/Refinery)
features.notes: Lev has supervisor pattern but no named multi-tier watchdog.

features.name: Daemon supervisor (Go select{} loop on tickers + signals)
features.notes: Same shape; lev's Tick is more semantically rich, gastown's heartbeat is more concrete.

features.name: Capacity-controlled dispatch (max_polecats + batch + spawn_delay)
features.lev_equivalent: no first-class capacity control in scheduler
features.notes: Lev's daemon worker pool has limits but no exposed capacity contract.

features.name: External LLM CLIs run in tmux panes (not in-process)
features.notes: Daemon does not embed LLMs — it spawns Claude Code/Codex/Gemini/Cursor etc. as subprocesses in tmux sessions. Communication via tmux send-keys, pane capture, mail, hook beads.

features.name: ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC types
features.lev_equivalent: poly handlers expose contracts but no ACP-shape protocol
features.notes: Could be poly's missing protocol layer for provider-runtime calls.

features.name: Dog (background helper task with own ticker)
features.notes: Per-task tickers for periodic helpers (compactor, stuck-agent, sheriff).

features.name: Plugin file-drop discovery (TOML+md+sh+go)
features.lev_equivalent: plugins/* with config.yaml + ts handlers via core/poly extension-registry
features.notes:
Lev plugin model is heavier (TS/build/contracts). gastown's md+sh+go+TOML
drop is much lower friction for ad-hoc automations. Worth lev/plugins/light.

features.name: Plugin gate types (cooldown/cron/event/condition/manual)
features.notes: Clean unification of scheduling + event-driven + manual triggers.

features.name: exec-wrapper plugin type (sandbox-exec / exitbox)
features.notes: Important for production multi-agent safety. Lev has no analogue.

features.name: Town/rig plugin override hierarchy
features.lev_equivalent: fractal config: system < global < project < module < env

features.name: AgentPresetInfo JSON registry (4-tier provider integration)
features.lev_equivalent: core/harness has provider abstraction; lighter shape, fewer presets
features.notes:
Most polished part of gastown. The 4-tier model is a clean spec lev's harness
could adopt verbatim. Pattern A/B/C hook variants are particularly useful.

features.name: Hook installer (Pattern A/B/C)
features.lev_equivalent: OMC hooks system covers some of this for Claude Code only
features.notes: Pattern A: claude-style settings.json with SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/ PreToolUse/Stop hooks → calls gt prime + gt mail check --inject + gt costs record. Pattern B: opencode JS plugin in .opencode/plugins/gastown.js. Pattern C: informational instructions.md nudged via tmux for Copilot-style.

features.name: Built-in plugins (rebuild-gt, dolt-snapshots, github-sheriff, quality-review, stuck-agent-dog, etc.)
features.lev_equivalent: plugins/sentinel, plugins/watchdog overlap; no curated automation library
features.notes: ~14 production plugins shipped in-repo as scheduled automations.

features.name: Fractal config (Town → Rig → Repo → Role TOML)
features.lev_equivalent: system < global < project < module < env (lev) — same idea, different naming
features.notes: 4-tier cascade: TownSettings (settings/config.json) → RigSettings → repo .gastown/settings.json → role TOML preset. Plus CLI flags + env at top.

features.name: Role TOML presets (mayor/deacon/witness/refinery/polecat/crew/dog)
features.lev_equivalent: no role-DNA tier in fractal config
features.notes: Pairs with gt-09 role taxonomy. Together they're ~80% of gastown's coordination model.

features.name: Replace-with-fallback override rule
features.notes: First non-empty wins per-key; nil-safe accessors fall through.

features.name: Multi-prefix env convention (GT_*/GASTOWN_*/BD_*/BEADS_*)
features.notes: GT_ROLE/GT_RIG/GT_ROOT/GT_TOWN_ROOT/GT_HOME/GT_SESSION/GT_DOLT_PORT/ GT_COST_TIER + GASTOWN_ENABLED/GASTOWN_DISABLED feature flags.

features.name: NOT XDG-compliant
features.lev_equivalent: lev IS XDG-compliant — this is a lev strength to preserve
features.notes: Uses ~/gt or $GT_HOME directly, ignores XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME.

features.name: Env passthrough allowlist (anti-contamination)
features.notes: Subtle but important for multi-provider safety.

features.name: Sling (assign work onto someone's hook)
features.lev_equivalent: no named primitive; closest is plugins/samurai dispatch
features.notes: Pairs with hook (gt-04). Together they form the cleanest dispatch primitive in the survey.

features.name: Mail (persistent addressed message queue)
features.lev_equivalent: events.jsonl is observation-only; no addressed mail channel
features.notes: Worth borrowing. Lev event-bus is the wrong shape for inter-agent messages.

features.name: Nudge (ephemeral tmux send-keys to peer)
features.lev_equivalent: tmux-harness can do this but no named verb
features.notes: Immediate ephemeral peer message via tmux pane send-keys.

features.name: Handoff (session-to-session refresh inside same identity)
features.notes: `/handoff` slash command refreshes a session's context without changing identity. Used at compaction boundaries.

features.name: Prime (inject role/mail/hooked-work context)
features.lev_equivalent: context loading via dna/ + skill load — less centralized
features.notes: Single-call context injection is cleaner than lev's distributed loading.

features.name: PreToolUse guard hook (gates PR creation, etc.)
features.lev_equivalent: OMC hooks but no production tool-guard contract
features.notes: `gt tap guard pr-workflow` invoked from claude-style PreToolUse hook. Fires before specific tool executions; can refuse.

features.name: No tribunal/consensus/vote primitive
features.lev_equivalent: lev has tribunal patterns — preserve as lev advantage
features.notes: gastown is dispatch+messaging, no deliberation; lev has /pov, /ralplan, /ccg.

features.name: Dolt SQL versioned state (branchable per-polecat)
features.notes:
Highest-leverage borrow. Branchable state is a major capability lev lacks.
Could replace/augment .lev/pm/workstreams. Dolt is Apache 2.0.

features.name: JSONL event log with Visibility (audit/feed/both)
features.lev_equivalent: .lev/events.jsonl exists but no audit/feed split, no curator
features.notes: ~/gt/.events.jsonl + ~/gt/.feed.jsonl — append-only, file-locked. Event schema: {ts, source, type, actor, payload, visibility[]}. Curator goroutine promotes audit→feed.

features.name: Curator daemon (audit→feed promotion)
features.notes: Background goroutine filters/promotes events to user-visible feed.

features.name: Crash-recovery checkpoint (.polecat-checkpoint.json)
features.lev_equivalent: core/lifecycle sha256 receipts, but no per-agent checkpoint shape
features.notes: Per-polecat JSON file written at session boundary: {molecule_id, current_step, modified_files, last_commit, branch, hooked_bead, session_id}. Next session resumes from this on crash/timeout/context-limit.

features.name: Memory typed beads (feedback/project/user/reference/general)
features.lev_equivalent: OMC project memory categories + core/memory hybrid system
features.notes: Memory categories stored as memory.* keys in beads/Dolt.

features.name: Atomic file writes (write-tmp + rename)
features.lev_equivalent: lev does atomic writes per-file; not a packaged primitive
features.notes: internal/atomicfile package; sole pattern for non-Dolt JSON state.

features.name: Cobra-based CLI with 60+ commands in 7 groups
features.notes: gastown CLI feels more curated; lev surface is broader but flatter.

features.name: Bubbletea TUI (`gt feed` flagship dashboard)
features.lev_equivalent: core/ui has UniversalWidget but no flagship realtime TUI
features.notes: gt feed is the most-cited operator UI in docs. Lev should have one.

features.name: Rebrandable binary (GT_COMMAND env)
features.notes: rootCmd.Use is dynamic via GT_COMMAND env — supports white-label aliases.

features.name: Cobra prefix matching (gt ref at = gt refinery attach)
features.lev_equivalent: no prefix matching in poly CLI surface
features.notes: Trivial to enable; nice ergonomic win.

features.name: Three auxiliary binaries (gt + gt-proxy-client + gt-proxy-server)
features.lev_equivalent: lev binary tree is poly-only; no proxy split
features.notes: Multi-binary distribution for sandbox/container scenarios.

features.name: ZERO programmatic SDK (intentional)
features.lev_equivalent: lev has poly with 5 surfaces (CLI/MCP/HTTP/WS/gRPC) — preserve as advantage
features.notes: gastown's SDK gap is lev's biggest moat in this comparison.

features.name: mTLS proxy server (cmd/gt-proxy-server :9876)
features.lev_equivalent: no analogue — lev assumes trusted runtime
features.notes: Important for production sandbox scenarios. Pairs with gt-32 (exec-wrapper).

features.name: Local-only admin API (127.0.0.1:9877)
features.notes: /v1/admin/issue-cert, /v1/admin/deny-cert — cert lifecycle.

features.name: OTel emitter with documented schema
features.lev_equivalent: core/telemetry exists but no published schema or event taxonomy
features.notes:
Best-documented OTel schema in the survey. Lev should publish equivalent
docs/otel-data-model.md for its event taxonomy.

features.name: run.id UUID waterfall correlation
features.notes: Each agent spawn gets a UUID propagated via GT_RUN env to subprocesses, surfaced as gt.run_id in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES for child bd processes. Cross-process correlation without distributed tracing.

features.name: NPM package = installer shim only
features.lev_equivalent: lev npm packages are real packages — preserve
features.notes: bin/gt.js spawns native binary; postinstall.js downloads tarball.

features.name: Imperative Go validation gates (distributed)
features.notes: Lev's declarative gate engine is materially better. Do NOT regress.

features.name: Feature flags via env vars (in-recorder enforcement)
features.lev_equivalent: lev has env flags but no in-recorder enforcement layer
features.notes: GT_LOG_AGENT_OUTPUT / GT_LOG_BD_OUTPUT / GT_LOG_PANE_OUTPUT etc. opt-in. "Enforced here so callers can't bypass it" pattern in RecordAgentEvent.

features.name: No constitutional/dna layer
features.notes: gastown has docs/design/property-layers.md + .golangci.yml + ci.yml as governance, but no dna/ equivalent — no constraint manifold, no entity ontology, no progressive-disclosure index.

features.name: Container-isolated e2e (Dockerfile.e2e)
features.lev_equivalent: lev CI is lighter; no container-isolated e2e harness
features.notes: golang:1.26-alpine + tmux + dolt + bd + gh, runs full integration suite in CI nightly. Multi-workflow GitHub Actions split (ci/nightly/e2e/windows/release).

features.name: LLM eval suite (gt-model-eval/promptfooconfig.yaml)
features.notes: promptfoo-driven evaluations of role prompts (witness, etc.).

features.name: Property tests (convoy_property_test.go = 13 t.Run blocks)
features.notes: Property-style invariant testing for convoy lifecycle.

features.name: ZFC (Zero Framework Cognition) coupling principle
features.lev_equivalent: lev poly is similar (handlers don't know surfaces)
